completion_criteria.text: U1-U7 experiments run and recorded in a companion findings doc; each claim marked verified or refuted with evidence, before any step that depends on it
Step 0 shipped: protect-claude-config.sh narrowed to the gate implementation and deny list only, ask converted to deny, confirmed live
Promotion manifest hardened first: hooks and permissions.deny reclassified so absence refuses promotion rather than deleting from live, and undeclared keys are refused instead of freezing
Delivery path proven without the sandbox: an agent pushes a branch and opens a PR through the centralized pr-create tool with no human hands
Layer 1 made operational: the two PreToolUse hooks registered in tracked settings and promoted to the live install, so checkpointing and rm-to-trash can fire at all
Install topology returned to direct repo symlinks: the ten ~/.claude entries point straight at the repo, and releases/, current, LIVE and local/ are removed
Deny pruned to genuine catastrophes per 0409 and every ask rule retired: entries that are speed bumps or routing preferences removed, user-affirmed gates and secret guards kept
Allow widened per 0408 so ordinary work never prompts: broad tool-level allow plus mcp__* coverage, and settings.local.json truncated so one-off rules stop accumulating at source
Layer 1 shipped whole: per-worktree temp-index checkpoint using --force, rm-to-trash rewrite, hourly APFS snapshot, and the D2 age-based reaper in the same change
Layer 3 shipped: one PreToolUse gate, P0-P6 in order, allow/block only, fail-open except P1/P2/P5, honoring the D3 local-container carve-out
Layer 4 shipped: append-only tool-call audit log plus a SessionStart heartbeat asserting layers 0 and 1 and the promotion pointer
Layer 0 shipped: sandbox with allowLocalBinding, allowUnsandboxedCommands false and failIfUnavailable true, keeping filesystem containment with working localhost
Step 8 shipped: the inert and harmful hooks deleted, the gate's dead release-tree tokens pruned with the suite green, and the dead nested settings.local.json removed
R3 rule change landed: the standing --dangerously-skip-permissions prohibition replaced by a rule requiring layers 0, 1 and 4 live first
Release path closed: a staleness heartbeat reports when local main is behind the remote without applying, and a verify verb asserts installed machinery matches its tracked source
Governed unattended launcher: a version-controlled script is the sole entry point, hardcodes the permission mode, and passes through no caller settings, closing the inline-JSON argv channel
One PR per MSP opened through the centralized pr-create tool, each leaving its base branch green
Gate rewritten to allow by default so unattended runs stop prompting: catastrophe branches and both PR denies kept, a hosted-Supabase deny added, Edit/Write/NotebookEdit given an allow hook

spine.active_goal: Closed. The permission architecture is shipped, merged and live; the bash gate allows by default and only catastrophe, PR and Supabase branches remain.
spine.next_step: Thread closed - no next step. If the work is reopened, worst first: the logbook fail-closed guard in the plugin repo, the only outstanding item that can freeze an overnight run; then measure whether a deny rule survives bypassPermissions, now the only control left on the PR and Supabase surfaces; then read the two dirty worktrees and decide what to keep.
spine.last_session: Rewrote the bash gate to allow by default (PR #99, main at 8ed7ed45), added a hosted-Supabase deny and a write-tool allow hook, retired G4 in full, then swept 13 branches and 7 worktrees. Gate suite 267 pass. The mitosis-os-process worktree was verified intact.

open_risks.text: Do not strip the merge gates or the pr-create centralization — they survive by the owner's deliberate choice rather than by the catastrophe test, so a future pruning pass will examine them and conclude wrongly

An agent can rewrite or delete the gate that judges it, in one unattended command — G4 is retired in full, so every guardrail-file write allows; git is the only recovery and nothing reports the change until a human looks

The logbook PreToolUse guard still fails closed and will freeze an unattended run — the wrapper turns any internal exception into a deny across Bash, Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit, hooks run in every permission mode, and dev 0.2.5 is byte-identical to the installed 0.2.4 on that file

Measure whether a deny rule survives the bypassPermissions mode before trusting an unattended run — deny is now the only control left on the PR and Supabase surfaces, and no experiment covers whether it holds in that mode

Nothing prevents a direct push to main any more — the literal-prefix denies were deleted and the gate never had a push clause, so publish-only-through-a-PR is a convention the tooling no longer enforces

Measure whether allow-write-tools.sh and secret-scanner.sh conflict on Edit and Write — both are PreToolUse hooks that return a decision, and deny beating allow is inference here rather than something this session measured

Apply every permission edit to BOTH the tracked and the live settings.json by hand — they are independent real files with no propagation path left, so an edit to one alone is inert; the reasoning for keeping them separate is in the decision record

Check which branch is checked out before trusting the live config — the ten entries symlink into the working tree, so the checked-out branch IS the live global configuration, and checking out an older one silently restores its hooks and permission rules

The permission mode is session-selected and nothing in the repository asserts it — defaultMode is null in all three settings files, so auto mode can be reselected silently; hooks now cover Bash and the write tools, but the MCP and read-tool allow entries stay exposed to the discard

Add a line to the MCP allow rules whenever an MCP server is added — an allow rule cannot use a bare mcp__* wildcard, so the twenty per-server entries are an enumeration with gaps by construction and a new server prompts until it is listed
The ledger server cannot run git, so reconcile fails with spawn git ENOENT — branch and binding drift is never folded, and every preflight since has briefed from unreconciled state

Two merged worktrees hold uncommitted work that exists nowhere else — fervent-cerf-833733 has five modified files and hermetic-guard-test has one, and neither diff was read before they were deliberately left standing

Fix or retire scripts/install_config.sh before anyone runs it by reflex — running it would undo the symlink topology and move the live global settings.json into a backup directory, replacing it with a repo symlink
Two SPEC documents still name session-config-drift-check.sh, deleted in 5ae9c24 — they were left as historical records, but a fresh session reading them will take the hook for live machinery

Re-check the ten symlinks after heavy subagent use — spawning subagents has destroyed the promoted entries before and the cause was never found; recovery is one ln -sfn loop since they are plain symlinks

key_decisions.title: Default-branch push denies stay, reclassified as delivery contract not catastrophe
Oversight-reducing changes wait for direct user confirmation
main is published only through a pull request, never a direct push
The containment architecture is removed; autonomy is a permissions problem only
A deny entry is removed when it guards no catastrophe; no replacement is required
Allow is broad by default; deny is the only narrow list
The ten entries are installed as explicit absolute symlinks, not through install_config.sh
The governed unattended launcher is struck; only a convenience wrapper survives
Auto mode is off, and allow deliberately carries both the broad and the narrow shape
R6 moves to the logbook plugin repository as a code defect
The live settings.json stays a separate hand-synced file rather than a symlink
The bash gate allows by default; only device, privileged-delete, exfiltration, PR and Supabase branches survive
The chflags nouchg branch is removed, retiring G4 in full

out_of_scope: Re-running any U1-U7 experiment - all seven are resolved with evidence in the findings doc, and re-running them costs hours and risks tripping the security flags that already fired twice
Pruning the refs under refs/checkpoint-experiment/ - deleting the refs is trivial, but reclaiming the space needs git gc --prune, which is irreversible and stays a human act
